newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU forecast for '97 German deficit at 3.2 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU forecast for '97 German deficit at 3.2 pct - paper.

text.p: The European Commission's twice-yearly economic forecasts for 1997 is expected show Germany's budget deficit at 3.2 percent of GDP, a Portuguese newspaper reported on Thursday.
The report, published in the newspaper Publico, also showed Italy's 1997 budget deficit projected at 3.8 percent of GDP, above the Maastricht treaty's 3.0 percent reference level.
For France and Spain, the Commission forecast showed both countries meeting the Maastricht target.
A representative from the newspaper told Reuters that the figures had been obtained from the Commission.
Responding to the article, a Commission spokesman said: "We have nothing to do with the table. Work on the forecast is still continuing."
The Commission is scheduled to release its twice-yearly forecasts on April 23.
When asked whether the table was wrong, the spokesman said: "We never make any comment on this sort of press speculation."
Economic and budget figures for 1997 will be used in assessing whether countries qualify for the single currency, expected in 1999.
